questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to an English-speaking country as I thought this was a bit easier and I wanted to improve and use my English. Furthermore, I looked at the different universities I could choose and Bath university looked like a great university with a lot of interesting subjects to choose from and a lot of different social things and societies to join. The social aspect was a really important parameter for me as well, because it would make it easier to socialise and meet new people.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
My overall study abroad period was amazing. The best thing for me was all the new friends I met in Bath, especially the other Erasmus students from all around the world. Furthermore, Bath is a really cozy beautiful little city and has a great location for doing trips to other cities around Bath. University of Bath was really great as well, with many different courses to choose from, a lot of facilities like the sport training village and loads of different student societies to join. 
The only negative thing about my study abroad was the laboratory work and my subject of my bachelor. I did not get any projects/subjects too choose from for my bachelor, so I ended up with a little weird subject that did not really fell into my interest. Apart from that the instruments in the laboratory were really old and did not always work properly and therefore I felt like I did a lot of the same work 3-4 times instead of just 1 time and even then, the results seemed a bit untrustworthy and I did not really feel I got as much out of it as I could since I did a lot of the same work in the laboratory.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy enough it just took some time to read everything and find the information you needed because there were a lot of thing you needed to know upon arrival. But overall it was quite easy and the student coordinator from Bath was really helpful. There were even created a whatsapp group chat for all the incoming students and two zoom meetings before arriving to ask questions and so on before arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was introduced to my accommodation when I arrived. At the university we had one introduction day where we got a tour at the university and a lot of different information. I also had a meeting with the some of the teachers from the pharmacy department where they helped with course registration and explained a bit about the courses I was going to take.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was really easy to find the student accommodation through the university. I just got an email about when to sign up for it and then I got allocated a room in the middle of December. There were two student accommodations that I could sign up for as an exchange student and they were both located in the city center.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived in Pulteney Court which was a great student accommodation, located 15 min by bus from the uni and 10 min walk from the city center. I got my own room which was fine and then I shared two bathrooms with 3 other flat mates and shared a kitchen with 7 other people which most of the time was super cozy. There were also a common room you could use to watch movies or drink a beer with you flat mates before going out. When arriving I had to buy all the kitchenware by myself, but you can share with your flat mates and buy a lot of cheap things in Poundland.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was quite easy. I got an email with the things I needed to do, like log on to their registration website and so on and then when I had the meeting with the staff from the pharmacy department in the introduction period, they enrolled my in all the courses I had chosen from home so I did not really do that myself.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I looked in the course catalogue when choosing the courses and talked a bit with the teachers of the courses I chose at the meeting in the introduction period. The mobility office was really helpful on email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look at the different courses in the course catalogue at the university's homepage and have some courses ready if you don´t get your first priorities. On the course catalogue you can see what kind of exams it is and what the learning outcomes is.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The level of the courses was similar to the courses in Denmark. Before going I was afraid that it was going to be really difficult, but the level was really similar to what is expected at KU.
In my bachelor´s project it was a lot of individual and independent work which was a bit scary in the beginning, but I learned a lot during that process and I could always ask my supervisor if I was lost.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There is a lot fewer lectures that at UCPH and no laboratory work at all. Besides the lectures the students are expected to read a lot of scientific articles about the different topics and some novel approaches within the subject. These articles are provided in the powerpoint slides. They record almost all the lectures which is really great in the revision period.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer:
The molecular biology and treatment of cancer
Global health and management
Research project

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked both of my courses. Global health and management were interesting and it was really nice since the exam form was 100% courses work during the semester so I only had one exam in the exam period. I also found the molecular biology and treatment of cancer really interesting and I would recommend both of these courses to future students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Bath uni had so many societies or clubs you can join through the student's union. Almost no matter which interest you have, I am sure you can find a club which matches. A lot of different sports societies like dance, gymnastics and tennis to the fine arts club, musical club and wine club.
Furthermore, the student's union arranged trips to the nearby cities like Oxford.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined the dance society, gymnastics, fine arts club, swam in the swimming pool and used the tennis courts. I would recommend all of those things.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit some of the nearby cities like Oxford, Bristol and Cardiff. Take a walk around in Bath, which is such a beautiful city. Visit the roman baths, go and have cream tea at Pulteney bridge, go to Alexandra park and watch the sunset, do the skyline walk, play cards with your new friends on the lawn in front of the royal crescent, go to the Hare and Hounds and eat Sunday roast and go and watch a musical in Bristol or London.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, British people are quite similar to Danish people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a club! I did ballet classes and gymnastics where I got to talk to some of the local students, but overall it was a bit hard because I only had 2-4 lectures every week and spent a lot of time alone in the laboratory.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The British students are really friendly and nice when you get to talk to them.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't be afraid that it is gonna be too hard, it will be worth it!
Attend all the social things you can and join a club to get new friends and socialise.
Just enjoy the beautiful city and all the nice possibilities Bath uni has to offer.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The process seems a bit complicated from the beginning with a lot of papers and so on, but it is really worth it to go and the mobility office at Bath Uni are really helpfull.
All the other exchange students are really nice and always up for doings something funny and at the end of your semester you will have friends all around the world.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the new friends and new people and cultures I got to meet.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To prioritise between doing school work and doing fun things with my friends.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
